title: Potato tuber moth on Irish potato - Zambia

Header: Potato tuber moth on Irish potato - Zambia

Prevention: Select healthy seed tubers, discard any infested tubers.
Plant deeper (more than 5cm) and hill up so that pests do not reach the tubers.
Avoid rotating in a field where a crop from the same plant family was grown previously, e.g. tomatoes, eggplants, pepper, or potatoes.
Destroy waste tubers, re-growing abandoned potato plants and residues from previous potato plantings.
Promote natural enemies by growing flowering plants around the field, or by not removing flowering weeds and reducing the number of insecticide sprays.
Avoid the use of potato leaves for mulch-covering tubers.
Mulch with neem leaves to repel the pest.
Intercrop with chillies, onions and garlic to repel the pest.
Irrigate lightly every 4 days during the last 5 weeks before harvest, irrigation must be stopped 1-2 days before harvesting.
Moist soil will reduce pest penetration to reach tubers.
Harvest immediately (and complete) when crop is mature.
Monitoring: Use pheromone traps in the field (several per ha) and check them weekly.
They have a narrow, silver-grey body and greyish-brown wings with tiny dark spots.
Scout fields until 6 weeks before harvesting and look for mines in the leaves, leaf stalks, stems and tunnels in the tuber.
The pests' damaging stage is the larvae (<1cm) which are grey, creamy or pale green with a dark brown head.
On leaves, thin mines appear because of feeding larvae.
On tubers, larvae are difficult to detect because they are inside.
During storage, check the stored tubers every two weeks.
If you see frass and holes in the tubers, then check for tunnels inside.
Direct Control: Remove infested tubers in storage and destroy them (e.g. by feeding to animals).
Foliar spray against the larvae, on the leaves.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, and restricted re- entry interval.
Do not empty into drains and water sources.
Highly toxic to water organisms, spiders and beetles.
Foliar spray against the larvae, when mining the leaves.
Before storing seed tubers, treat them with 5% malathion dust.
